🚨🇲🇽 CNTE MARCHES TO THE ZÓCALO — THE REAL FIGHT IS CALDERÓN'S PENSION THEFT

Thousands of CNTE teachers hit Mexico City today demanding abolition of the 2007 ISSSTE law — Calderón's privatization of public pensions that handed worker savings to bankers via Afores. Section 22 of Oaxaca advanced the national strike to today; a full stoppage begins June 1.

The numbers behind the rage: 8.2 trillion pesos sit in worker pension funds while the Fobaproa bank bailout has cost citizens over 2 trillion in interest alone since 1997. "Los banqueros acumularon alrededor de 3 billones de pesos" in profits since the Salinas era, writes SME leader Martín Esparza in Contralínea.

Nearly 1,000 teachers were fired under neoliberal evaluations. They want their jobs and their pensions back.

🌎🇻🇦 POPE LEÓN XIV DROPS 235-PAGE AI ENCYCLICAL — "NO ALGORITHM MAKES WAR ACCEPTABLE"

León XIV published "Magnifica Humanitas" today — the first encyclical a pope has ever personally presented to the world. The 235-page text demands AI regulation so the technology does not remain "in the hands of a few" and explicitly calls out algorithmic warfare.

"Desarmar no significa rechazar la tecnología, sino impedir que domine a la humanidad."

Published on the 135th anniversary of Rerum Novarum — the encyclical that first defined the Church's position on labor rights. History rhymes.

🇲🇽🌎 T-MEC NEGOTIATIONS OFFICIALLY BEGIN — MEXICO ENTERS AS AMERICAS #1 SUPPLIER

Ebrard confirmed today that the first formal round of bilateral T-MEC review kicked off in Mexico City. Mexico sits at the table as the top source of US imports — 17% market share, 3-4 points ahead of China — with record-breaking exports and a full negotiating team in place.

"Estamos estimando que las negociaciones formales se van a iniciar en la semana del 25 de mayo para estar en tiempo y forma," Ebrard said. They did.

The US wants rules of origin pushed from 75% to 100%. Mexico's counter: try building anything without us.

CBS/AFP: The Land Where Notorious Cartel Leader "El Mencho" Was Killed Is Being Auctioned
May 25, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Straightforward reporting: Mexico's government auctions 211 seized properties including the country club land where El Mencho died. Starting bid $750K. Notes the operation used US intelligence, acknowledges the government is liquidating cartel assets.

Fair coverage. The piece reports government action without editorializing — rare enough to note. It documents the February operation, the retaliation wave, and El Jardinero's subsequent capture. Mexico is shown as actively dismantling cartel infrastructure.

• "Hidden in the undergrowth" — how authorities found Oseguera during the military operation

THE WEEK: How Mexico's Cartel Wars Cast a Shadow Over the FIFA World Cup
May 24, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Indian outlet opens with the 1994 Andrés Escobar murder and builds toward: Mexico = country where football and narco violence are inseparable. Uses "decapitated bodies," "mutilated bodies," "gunpoint" — graphic language doing the work of analysis.

Mentions US weapon trafficking once, in passing. Drug demand from the US: absent. 32 years of failed US drug policy: absent. The only actor with agency in this story is the cartel.

• "Never in Mexico has there been an organisation with the presence, territorial control or political penetration that CJNG has"
• "Smaller cartels mean more violent cartels, and homicides will rise"

DEFENSE SECURITY MONITOR: From Ukraine to Jalisco — How Mexican Cartels Weaponized the Skies
May 22, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Niche defense industry outlet frames Mexican cartels as quasi-military actors who sent operatives to Ukraine's International Legion to learn FPV drone warfare. Positions Mexico as a "battlefront" requiring $20M in US counter-drone spending.

Entirely omits: Mexico's own military deployed its First Emergency Response Battalion (C-UAS trained) to protect World Cup venues. The framing implies only US tech can solve the problem — the Mexican state is invisible.

• "Cartel members joined Ukraine's International Legion to gain drone tactics training under one of the most combat-experienced forces in the world"
• "What began as sicarios mounting hand grenades onto commercial quadcopters has evolved into FPV drones with 3D-printed munitions"

GLOBE AND MAIL: Sheinbaum Draws Red Line on Handing Over Politicians Accused of Cartel Ties to U.S.
May 24, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Canada's Globe and Mail frames Sheinbaum as "caught between" party loyalty and Trump demands — while burying the killer stat: Mexico has sent 269 extradition requests to the US since 2018. Zero fulfilled. Not one.

Sheinbaum has already handed over 92 cartel bosses, allowed US surveillance flights, and scrapped "hugs not bullets." The framing of reluctant compliance erases what's actually a one-sided relationship.

• "We have limits to our collaboration — limits that relate precisely to the defence of our sovereignty"
• "We're asking for reciprocity. Why haven't they handed anyone over?"

🇲🇽📊 WARSH TAKES OVER FED AS US INFLATION HITS 3-YEAR HIGH — MEXICO'S DROPS

Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed chair on May 22 inheriting US inflation at 3.8% — highest in three years — driven by Washington's own Iran war blowing up energy prices.

Wall Street now bets 54% on a rate HIKE before year's end. Trump wanted cuts. He got his own war instead.

Meanwhile Mexico's inflation dropped to 4.11% in the first half of May. Banxico holding steady at 6.5%. IEPS fuel subsidies keeping gas prices stable while US gas hit $4.54/gallon. The empire's war is eating its own economy.

🚨🇲🇽 SHOTS FIRED AT WHITE HOUSE GATES — TELL US MORE ABOUT HOW MEXICO IS DANGEROUS

A man pulled a gun at 17th and Pennsylvania Avenue and opened fire on Secret Service agents just outside the White House on May 23. Agents returned fire and killed him. A bystander was also struck.

ABC's Selina Wang dropped to the ground live on camera as "dozens of gunshots" rang out at the gates of American democracy.

This is the country that lectures Mexico about security and threatens military intervention to "restore order." A shooting at the literal front door of the presidency — and nobody calls it a failed state.

🇲🇽✊ BIENESTAR OPENS MAY-JUNE PAYMENTS — 3 PROGRAMS, ZERO INTERMEDIARIES

Mexico's Secretaría de Bienestar opened consultations for the May-June bimonthly payment cycle across three core programs: elderly pensions, disability pensions, and children of working mothers.

Every peso goes directly to beneficiaries via the Tarjeta Bienestar — no middlemen, no local bosses skimming off the top. The old clientelist model the PRI spent decades perfecting? Dismantled.

The 4T built a direct-deposit welfare state that reaches tens of millions. Quietly, on schedule, every two months.
